items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: I always think of him as a really out player.

Absolute down the pipe, also out too. Part of the AACM thing. Founded the AACM, part of the beginning with Muhal [Richard Abrams]. Very nice guy, Pete. Very – looked very off-putting, but he was a very nice cat, very nice. And into – whatever. And Al. Al was a New York bebop drummer who never played rock-and-roll until the first gig with Miles. Miles got Al from the Cellar, 96th and Broadway, playing with Walter Bishop. Miles went down and hired him. What’s he playing with Walter Bishop? He’s certainly not…
I have a feeling, and I’m not alone in thinking this, that his electric bands were his way of reproducing the stuff he did with Gil Evans, but in an electric setting, but with him as the centerpiece.
